chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha', from Abdullah ibn 'Ajlan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) — regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic:
'So ask the people of the Reminder if you do not know' [16:43]
He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: The Reminder is I, and the Imams are the People of the Reminder.
And regarding His words, Mighty and Majestic: 'And indeed it is a reminder/honor for you and for your people, and you will soon be questioned' [43:44]
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: We are his people, and we are the ones who will be questioned.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الذِّكْرِ: People of the Reminder — in Shia interpretation, refers to the Prophet and Imams, not merely scholars in general
key_terms.الذِّكْرُ: The Reminder — interpreted here as the Prophet himself, and by extension the Quran and divine guidance
key_terms.الْمَسْؤُولُونَ: Those who will be questioned — the Imams, as guardians of the divine message

ai.seo_question: Who are the Ahl al-Zikr (People of the Reminder) according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) interprets two Quranic verses to establish that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) himself declared 'I am the Reminder,' and that the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt are the 'People of the Reminder' (Ahl al-Zikr) whom believers are commanded to consult. The verse 43:44 is further interpreted to identify the Ahl al-Bayt as the Prophet's 'people' who will be held accountable for transmitting and guarding the divine message. This exegesis was addressed to a community navigating questions of religious authority after the Prophet, asserting that the living Imams — not the general scholarly class — are the authoritative interpreters of scripture.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhmmad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washha, from Abdullah Bin Ajlan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[16:43] so ask the People of the Reminder if you do not know.
Heasws said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww is the Zikr (Reminder). Iasws and the Imamsasws are the People of the Remider (Ahl Al-Zikr)’.
And (as for) the Words of the Mighty and Majestic [43:44] And it is a Reminder for you and your people, and you shall soon be questioned,
Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> are his<sup>saww</sup> people, and we<sup>asws</sup> would be asked (about the Divine matters)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from ’Abdallah ibn ‘Ajlan from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following about the words of Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High.
“Ask the people of Dhikr if you do not know.” (16:43, 21: 7 Holy Quran).
The Holy Prophet (s.a.) has said, ‘I am the Dhikr and the Imams are the people of Dhikr.’”
About the words of Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High that says, “It is a Dhikr for you and for your people and you all will be asked questions.’ [43:44]

The Imams (a.s.) said, “We are his people and we will be questioned.”(It seems that both the Holy Prophet (s.a.) is called Dhikr and the Holy Quran is also called Dhikr although the above passage seems confusing).
